fact: Angola's Justice Minister says the Bilhete de Identidade results from integrating data in the birth record through interoperability between the respective computer systems.

Angola's Ministry of Justice and Human Rights runs a Universalisation of Civil Registration and Identity Cards Programme, whose plan aims to give identity cards to all adult citizens listed in the civil registry database by December 2026, per National Director Aristides Marques.

Angola says changes to the civil registry and identity card laws led to operations to merge the two systems, and a multifunctional database under the Ministry of Justice holds the civil registry and identity card management systems.

Angop reports that Mbanza Kongo (Zaire) began civil registration of newborns with consequent attribution of the Bilhete de Identidade at a maternity post, under the nationwide EU-funded 'Nascer com Registo' project, running at the hospital since October 2025.

fact: Aristides Marques, national director of Identification, Registries and Notary, says a death registered through the conservatoria services is sent to the database to deregister (give baixa to) the citizen, which needs the deceased's BI to be reliable.

Secretary of State for Justice Osvaldo Amaro said the Plataforma Unica do Cidadao, integrating civil registration and the identity card (BI) so that they work as one, is in a very advanced stage of institutionalisation.
